utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, case number IT-95-14/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution, Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, thank you. Mr. Norman Farrell and Mr. Fabricio Guarglia for the Prosecution with Ms. Sue Grogan our case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: For the appellant, General Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, my name it Mitko Naumovski attorney from Zagreb for Mr. Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And for Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, my name is Bozidar Kovacic and I represent Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference called in accordance with the rules. I was handed, on my way into court, a document which has been filed - I assume it's been filed - it's dated the 10th of October. Unfortunately, the resources of our registry are such that I don't appear to have been given a copy of it but I have read it. I am very grateful to those who prepared it. Well, Mr. Farrell, I suppose it says everything, doesn't it? It's an agreed document as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So it says everything as to when things should be ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: As anticipated, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's a bit grim.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I must tell you, when we reviewed the material, we felt the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the size of it I can understand the problem. But if it's going to take that long, it's going to take that long, which means we'll have another Status Conference before the matter is ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Hopefully not, but it may take that long. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: One and a half million pages. What does that make the total up upstairs now? Four and a half million, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I think -- this is included in the -- I think it's 3.8 or something like that. But the stuff that's come in in the last while adds up to that amount since our last comprehensive search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there anything you wanted to add to what's in the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Anything that the Defence wishes to raise. It is a very unhappy position. But if that's the position, there is very little that can be done about it unless you've got some suggestions. Mr. Naumovski, what about you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Honour. I just explained to Mr. Kordic a few minutes what situation we are in. And the Defence has no choice but to accept the time scale and the situation we find ourselves in. If the Prosecution has really received an enormous number of documents numbering a million and a half pages, there is nothing else we can do but wait for them to look through the material and Defence will fill their obligations under Rule 68, Article 61.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I was hoping, I suppose, hope against hope that you may have some way of resolving it, but I can't see one myself. Is there anything you want to raise about your client's personal situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No thank you, Your Honour, Mr. Kordic has nothing special to raise with respect to his detention conditions and there are no other problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Anything on behalf of Mr. Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. I agree with what my colleagues have said, the problems seem to be of an objective nature, they are as they are. I only hope that we will not waste time waiting and then have a situation in which no documents of value turn up, but this is in God's hands. As for my client's status, there are no special problems but I have to say that I have been considering lodging a new motion for provisional release because it seems that this case can go on and on, because archive material from Bosnia and Croatia will continue to keep coming in. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, in response to what you say, I think I should point this out, that if you want the appeal to be heard on the material which you have now, it can be heard. But as I understand it, this material is likely to contain exculpatory material - at least some, what its will be worth, I don't know, it's a matter for you. It is exceedingly unfortunate that everything seems to be coming up so late in the case. But it's for you to determine whether you want to proceed with the material you have now or whether you want to see whether it turns up something important which will assist your client. It's not easy position for you to be in, but I don't want you to proceed upon the basis that you are forced to wait for anything. It's a matter for you. Now, is there anything that you want to raise in relation to your client's personal situation in custody?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No, there is nothing I wish to raise. I agree with everything you have said and, of course, it is for us to decide. But it's quite clear that as long as there is at least one per cent chance of our finding any exculpatory material for our client, of course we have to wait, which is why we are not raising any issues. The situation is such as it is. Unfortunately, however, this detention period has become very long indeed. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Farrell, just one minor compliant and it's not your fault, I know, but you have to realise that something happens in the registry here which is quite mystical, documents take longer to get to the Judges than it takes to get to anybody else in the Chamber. My legal assistant seems to get them at least 24 hours before I do, but even he hadn't received this one this morning. So I would suggest that you if you've got something immediately before a hearing of this nature, that you file it two days in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I'll endeavour to do so, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you all for coming and I'll adjourn.
